messages:
sara: Heads up — seeing a 2x tail latency spike on the Mixtral->Llama draft pairing during canary. Repro at seq_len=512, p95 goes from 120ms -> 260ms.

noah: Can you paste the perf profile and which attention kernel got chosen?

sara: Paste from live profiler: 
```
profile: model_pair: mixtral_v1 -> llama_v2
kernel_selected: fused_attention_v2 (mixtral)
fallback_kernel: generic_matmul (llama)
seq_len: 512
kv_writes/sec: 14k
kv_reads/sec: 28k
fallback_count: 42
avg_token_latency: 6.4ms -> 12.8ms
notes: extra copy on tokenizer handshake, token id remap hits ~3.2% of tokens
```

kai: That token id remap % is suspicious. Could be RoPE scaling mismatch forcing a tokenizer sanitization pass during handshake. Acceptance rate for speculative drafts down to 54%.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: canary deployment build-2312 completed at 2026-03-18T11:22Z :white_check_mark:

maria: Try forcing kernel selection to attn_experimental via runtime override for this family. Quick config: 
```json
{"runtime": {"kernel_policy": {"mixtral": "attn_experimental", "llama": "attn_experimental"}, "max_batch_size": 64}}
```

noah: I tried that on a small run — p95 improved ~25% but draft acceptance dropped further. Speculative decoder now generates more drafts and fallback_count increased.

sara: We think the root is tokenizer vocab offsets between families. Mixtral uses a different subword split for some fast-path tokens; our handshake runs an expensive remap table which invalidates KV prefetch.

kai: Can you dump mismatch samples (token pairs) and remap hits?

sara: quick sample: 
```
orig_tokens: [\"Ġthe\", \"Ġmodel\", \"▁\"]
mixtral_ids: [145, 2099, 3]
llama_ids: [145, 2105, 9]
remap_hits: {2105->2099: 312, 9->3: 48}
```

devex: For canary try dialing draft_accept_threshold up a bit and enable lightweight normalization pipeline: 
```yaml
runtime.experiments:
  draft_accept_threshold: 0.65
  tokenizer.fast_normalize: true
  kv_prefetch: true
```

noah: Also adjust batching heuristics: dynamic max_batch by family and prefer family-local batching to avoid cross-family kernel swaps. Something like: 
```
batching: {policy: family_affinity, max_batch_per_family: {mixtral: 48, llama: 64}}
```

sara: Kicking off an eng-runtime perf job: 1k sessions, collect [per_token_latency, acceptance_rate, fallback_count, kv_hits]. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/2113377700 (run queued).

infra-bot: perf-job-2113377700 finished: results available (run time 42m).

maria: Note on RoPE: Mixtral uses rope_alpha ~1.02 in the tokenizer/rope config vs ~1.0 for llama. When we pair drafts across families we need to normalize RoPE scaling or we see head drift and extra alignment ops in the runtime. That explains extra kernel conversions and slower KV reuse.

kai: I'll queue a kernel-selection sweep that includes quantized kernels and the attn_experimental path, measure fallback_count and kv_reuse_ratio.

noah: If kernel override helps p95 but hurts acceptance, we might need to treat acceptance_rate as a first-class SLO for draft routing. Tradeoff: lower latency vs more drafts -> higher overall compute.

sara: Agreed. For now I'll revert the canary to stable to remove tail latency from production. We'll iterate on the perf-job results and propose a runtime config that: 1) normalizes RoPE for mixed-family handshakes, 2) prefers family-local batches, 3) uses draft_accept_threshold tuning and kv_prefetch.

maria: Thanks — post results here when ready. Also file a follow-up for tokenizer remap cache (small LRU) so handshake doesn't pay full table cost every time. :memo:
